literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在7天内采集的两个鼻咽拭子样本均检测到RSV-B,两个样本中F:K68Q突变的等位基因频率均较高。 [10.1007/s40121-026-01442-0]
具有医学背景的受访者在回答关于RSV的问题时更常给出正确答案。例如,当被问及治疗RSV感染的方法时,109名医学专业人员(74.15%)回答正确,而251名非医学受访者(48.18%;p < 0.001)回答正确。 [10.17219/acem/212578]
在每获得一个 QALY 的阈值为 CLP15,977,348(US$17,180)的情况下,从卫生保健和社会视角分别得出最大成本有效的 疫苗 价格为 CLP100,480(US$108)和 CLP265,261(US$285)。 [10.1080/14760584.2026.2725347]
共获得302个RSV序列,其中72.7%的病例涉及下呼吸道感染,67.2%需要住院治疗,15.0%被转入重症监护病房(ICU)。此外,还识别出17例尼塞韦单抗突破性感染(N_BI),并发现四个大型系统发育簇(LPCs),其中包括2024–2025季节的两个新簇。 [10.1186/s13073-026-01768-x]

系统发育分析显示RSV-A株属于A.D.1、A.D.2、A.D.3谱系,RSV-B 基因组属于B.D.4.1、B.D.4.1.1、B.D.E.1、B.D.E.5和B.D.E.谱系。在两个季节监测期间,我们在RSV-A 基因组中发现了9个突变位点,在RSV-B 基因组中发现了18个突变位点。此外,我们在RSV-A和RSV-B 基因组中分别发现了7个和8个突变位点,这些突变位点位于G蛋白保守中央域。在2023-24和2024-25季节,我们分别观察到3例(6.7%)和27例(15.8%)病毒共感染。 [10.64898/2026.09.09.26362646]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Two nasopharyngeal samples collected 7 days apart were positive for RSV-B, with the F:K68Q substitution detected at high allele frequencies in both samples. [10.1007/s40121-026-01442-0]
Respondents with medical backgrounds more frequently provided correct answers to questions regarding RSV than those without medical training. [10.17219/acem/212578]

At a threshold of CLP15,977,348 (US$17,180) per QALY gained, the maximum cost-effective vaccine price was CLP100,480 (US$108) and CLP265,261 (US$285) from the healthcare and societal perspectives respectively. [10.1080/14760584.2026.2725347]

A total of 302 RSV sequences were retrieved, with 72.7% of cases involving lower-respiratory-tract infections, 67.2% requiring hospitalization, and 15.0% admitted to the intensive-care-unit (ICU). [10.1186/s13073-026-01768-x]

Phylogenetic analysis showed RSV-A strains belonged to the A.D.1, A.D.2, A.D.3 lineages, and RSV-B genomes belonged to the B.D.4.1, B.D.4.1.1, B.D.E.1, B.D.E.5, and B.D.E. [10.64898/2026.09.09.26362646]
literature.trend_or_risk_en: The direction of this week's research is defined by the clinical, epidemiological, ecological, diagnostic and molecular topics actually represented by the eligible publications.
literature.brief_en: This literature brief prioritizes papers published in the active reporting window and ranks them by relevance, evidence availability, study quality, recency, and independent-source convergence. Detailed study-specific evidence is retained in the article cards below.
brief_items_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
在7天内采集的两个鼻咽拭子样本均检测到RSV-B,两个样本中F:K68Q突变的等位基因频率均较高。 [10.1007/s40121-026-01442-0]。
具有医学背景的受访者在回答关于RSV的问题时更常给出正确答案。例如,当被问及治疗RSV感染的方法时,109名医学专业人员(74.15%)回答正确,而251名非医学受访者(48.18%;p < 0.001)回答正确。

papers.title: Detection of a Nirsevimab-Resistant RSV-B Variant (F:K68Q) in an Adult with Severe Infection.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is recognized as a major cause of severe disease in adults, particularly those having cardiorespiratory comorbidities or immunosuppression. The recent deployment of monoclonal antibodies targeting the prefusion F protein could be used in the future to prevent RSV-associated hospitalization and critical illness in immunocompromised adult patients. METHODS: This report is part of the ongoing ARF-RSV study (NCT06197152), a prospective, multicenter observational cohort. RESULTS: We report on the case of a 64-year-old man with a previous medical history of aggressive mantle cell lymphoma under active treatment who was admitted to the intensive care unit for severe sepsis in the setting of febrile aplasia. Clinical evolution was rapidly favorable, with resolution of hemodynamic failure within a few days. Two nasopharyngeal samples collected 7 days apart were positive for RSV-B. Genetic analysis identified a strain belonging to lineage B.D.E.1, with both samples harboring a dominant F:K68Q substitution in the fusion protein. In the first sample, the mean depth of coverage was over 180× and the F:K68Q substitution was detected at an allele frequency of 99%. In the second sample, collected 7 days later, the mean depth of coverage was 170×, with the same substitution detected with an allele frequency of 97%, consistent with persistence as a dominant variant over time. This substitution has been previously associated with high-level resistance to nirsevimab. More generally, F:K68Q appears to be rare among circulating RSV-B strains based on available global sequence surveillance data (GISAID). Its detection in a monoclonal antibody-naïve patient reinforces the hypothesis that this substitution may circulate independently of nirsevimab exposure. CONCLUSION: The persistence of a resistant RSV variant in a patient who was immunocompromised without prior exposure to nirsevimab suggests that such variants may circulate and be transmitted. In this context, RSV vaccination of patients who are immunocompromised may not only provide individual protection but also help limit the dissemination of resistant strains.

papers.title_zh: 检测到一名严重感染成人中具有尼塞韦单抗耐药性的RSV-B变异株(F:K68Q)
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is recognized as a major cause of severe disease in adults, particularly those having cardiorespiratory comorbidities or immunosuppression. The recent deployment of monoclonal antibodies targeting the prefusion F protein could be used in the future to prevent RSV-associated hospitalization and critical illness in immunocompromised adult patients. METHODS: This report is part of the ongoing ARF-RSV study (NCT06197152), a prospective, multicenter observational cohort. RESULTS: We report on the case of a 64-year-old man with a previous medical history of aggressive mantle cell lymphoma under active treatment who was admitted to the intensive care unit for severe sepsis in the setting of febrile aplasia. Clinical evolution was rapidly favorable, with resolution of hemodynamic failure within a few days. Two nasopharyngeal samples collected 7 days apart were positive for RSV-B. Genetic analysis identified a strain belonging to lineage B.D.E.1, with both samples harboring a dominant F:K68Q substitution in the fusion protein. In the first sample, the mean depth of coverage was over 180× and the F:K68Q substitution was detected at an allele frequency of 99%. In the second sample, collected 7 days later, the mean depth of coverage was 170×, with the same substitution detected with an allele frequency of 97%, consistent with persistence as a dominant variant over time. This substitution has been previously associated with high-level resistance to nirsevimab. More generally, F:K68Q appears to be rare among circulating RSV-B strains based on available global sequence surveillance data (GISAID). Its detection in a monoclonal antibody-naïve patient reinforces the hypothesis that this substitution may circulate independently of nirsevimab exposure. CONCLUSION: The persistence of a resistant RSV variant in a patient who was immunocompromised without prior exposure to nirsevimab suggests that such variants may circulate and be transmitted. In this context, RSV vaccination of patients who are immunocompromised may not only provide individual protection but also help limit the dissemination of resistant strains.

papers.title: Clinical and economic impact of bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F (RSVpreF) vaccination in older adults: a cost-effectiveness analysis for Chile.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of lower respiratory tract disease in older adults in Chile. Chile's National Immunization Technical Advisory Group (NITAG) recommended RSV vaccination for adults aged ≥60 years with risk factors for severe illness. This study estimated the cost-effectiveness of bivalent RSVpreF vaccination among at-risk older adults in Chile. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A population-based Markov model projected RSV-related outcomes under no vaccination and RSVpreF vaccination over the cohort lifetime. Cost-effectiveness was assessed from healthcare and societal perspectives in 2025 Chilean Pesos (CLP) and US Dollars (US$), with costs and outcomes discounted at 3% annually. Sensitivity analyses tested the model robustness. RESULTS: RSVpreF vaccination was projected to prevent 14,956 hospitalizations, 50,419 emergency department visits, and 124,849 physician office visits; avert CLP76 billion (US$82 million) in direct medical costs and CLP305 billion (US$328 million) in indirect costs; and generate 7,079 quality-adjusted life-years (QALYs). At a threshold of CLP15,977,348 (US$17,180) per QALY gained, the maximum cost-effective vaccine price was CLP100,480 (US$108) and CLP265,261 (US$285) from the healthcare and societal perspectives respectively. CONCLUSIONS: RSVpreF vaccination would reduce RSV burden and likely be cost-effective for older adults in Chile.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 成本效果分析从卫生保健和社会视角进行,以 2025 年智利比索(CLP)和美元(US$)为单位,成本和结果均按每年 3% 的折现率进行折现。
analysis_zh.methods: 研究设计与方法:基于人群的马尔可夫模型预测了在未接种 疫苗接种 和接种 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 的情况下,RSV 相关结果在 队列研究 生命期内的演变。
analysis_zh.main_results: 在每获得一个 QALY 的阈值为 CLP15,977,348(US$17,180)的情况下,从卫生保健和社会视角分别得出最大成本有效的 疫苗 价格为 CLP100,480(US$108)和 CLP265,261(US$285)。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: RSVpreF 疫苗接种预计可预防14,956例住院、50,419例急诊科就诊和124,849例医生诊所就诊;避免CLP76亿(US$82百万)的直接医疗费用和CLP305亿(US$328百万)的间接费用;并产生7,079个质量调整生命年(QALYs)。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: RSVpreF 疫苗接种 将减少 RSV 的负担,并可能在智利老年人中具有成本效益。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这种确定性提取基于检索到的全文证据。该消息来源没有明确报告独立评估的足够局限性,因此可信度较低。

papers.title: Molecular epidemiology of respiratory syncytial virus infections in Arizona, USA during the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons.
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus infection is a common cause of hospitalizations in infants and elderly patients. With the increased availability of vaccines and therapeutic antibodies, surveilling the sequence landscape of viral genomes is important to increase awareness of potentially neutralizing mutations. During the 2023-24 and 2024-25 RSV seasons, we collected unpaired nasopharyngeal swab specimens from patients presenting to Arizona healthcare systems with symptoms of influenza-like illness. Using either tiled amplicon-based enrichment or a commercial oligo hybrid-enrichment panel and next generation sequencing, we obtained genome sequences for RSV and co-infecting viruses. We performed phylogenetic and genomic analyses to classify RSV genomes and detect mutations in the antigenic sites of the F protein and conserved central domain of the G protein. Phylogenetic analysis showed RSV-A strains belonged to the A.D. 1, A.D.2, A.D.3, and A.D. RSV-B genomes belonged to the B.D.4.1, B.D.4.1.1, B.D.E.1, B.D.E.5, and B.D.E. We found 9 polymorphic sites located in the antigenic sites of the F protein in our RSV-A genomes and 18 polymorphic sites in our RSV-B genomes over the two-season surveillance period. We identified 7 polymorphic sites in our RSV-A genomes and 8 polymorphic sites in our RSV-B genomes that are in the conserved central domain of the G protein. We also discovered 3 (6.7%) and 27 (15.8%) incidences of viral coinfections in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 seasons, respectively. Viral genomic surveillance plays an important role in maintaining the efficacy of vaccine and therapeutic agents. Continued monitoring of circulating variants is an important component of public health.

source_records.title: Respiratory infections
source_records.abstract: Abstract Pneumonia is diagnosed based on clinical symptoms and radiological features. It can be caused by a variety of pathogens including bacterial, mycobacterial, viral, fungal, and other atypical organisms. Most bacterial community-acquired pneumonia is due to Streptococcus pneumoniae, which is normally treated with penicillin and can be risk stratified using the CURB-65 score. Atypical organisms require macrolides. Hospital-acquired pneumonia involves Gram-negative or resistant organisms and treatment depends on local sensitivities. Viral pneumonias can include influenza and COVID-19, with antivirals used only in specific cases. Immunocompromised patients may develop invasive fungal infections such as Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia or invasive aspergillosis requiring targeted antifungals.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在监测呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)基因组的序列景观,以提高对可能中和的突变的认识,鉴于抗呼吸道合胞病毒药物和治疗性抗体的可用性增加。这对于维持这些干预措施的有效性和公共卫生监测至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在2023-24和2024-25 RSV季节,我们从亚利桑那州医疗机构就诊并出现流感样症状的患者中收集了未配对的鼻咽拭子标本。
elements_zh.methods: 我们使用嵌合扩增子富集或商业寡核苷酸杂交富集面板和下一代测序获得了RSV和共感染病毒的基因组序列。我们进行了系统发育和基因组分析,以分类RSV 基因组,并检测F蛋白的抗原位点和G蛋白保守中央域中的突变。
elements_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析显示RSV-A株属于A.D.1、A.D.2、A.D.3谱系,RSV-B 基因组属于B.D.4.1、B.D.4.1.1、B.D.E.1、B.D.E.5和B.D.E.谱系。在两个季节监测期间,我们在RSV-A 基因组中发现了9个突变位点,在RSV-B 基因组中发现了18个突变位点。此外,我们在RSV-A和RSV-B 基因组中分别发现了7个和8个突变位点,这些突变位点位于G蛋白保守中央域。在2023-24和2024-25季节,我们分别观察到3例(6.7%)和27例(15.8%)病毒共感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了继续监测循环RSV变异株和检测可能中和的突变的重要性。这对于维持抗呼吸道合胞病毒药物和治疗剂的有效性至关重要。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 病毒基因组监测在维持抗呼吸道合胞病毒药物和治疗剂的有效性方面发挥着重要作用。继续监测循环变异株是公共卫生的重要组成部分。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括缺乏随机化和由于观察性研究可能导致的偏倚。样本量足以满足研究目标,但其普遍性可能仅限于亚利桑那州医疗机构。证据强度为中等。

analysis_zh.methods: 我们使用嵌合扩增子富集或商业寡核苷酸杂交富集面板和下一代测序获得了RSV和共感染病毒的基因组序列。我们进行了系统发育和基因组分析,以分类RSV 基因组,并检测F蛋白的抗原位点和G蛋白保守中央域中的突变。
analysis_zh.main_results: 系统发育分析显示RSV-A株属于A.D.1、A.D.2、A.D.3谱系,RSV-B 基因组属于B.D.4.1、B.D.4.1.1、B.D.E.1、B.D.E.5和B.D.E.谱系。在两个季节监测期间,我们在RSV-A 基因组中发现了9个突变位点,在RSV-B 基因组中发现了18个突变位点。此外,我们在RSV-A和RSV-B 基因组中分别发现了7个和8个突变位点,这些突变位点位于G蛋白保守中央域。在2023-24和2024-25季节,我们分别观察到3例(6.7%)和27例(15.8%)病毒共感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调了继续监测循环RSV变异株和检测可能中和的突变的重要性。这对于维持抗呼吸道合胞病毒药物和治疗剂的有效性至关重要。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 病毒基因组监测在维持抗呼吸道合胞病毒药物和治疗剂的有效性方面发挥着重要作用。继续监测循环变异株是公共卫生的重要组成部分。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 研究设计的局限性包括缺乏随机化和由于观察性研究可能导致的偏倚。样本量足以满足研究目标,但其普遍性可能仅限于亚利桑那州医疗机构。证据强度为中等。

papers.title: Burden and Risk Factors for Severe Respiratory Syncytial Virus Infection Among Pediatric Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial morbidity in pediatric hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients; however, risk factors for severe disease remain incompletely characterized. Methods We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study across 16 U.S. transplant centers, evaluating children and adolescents (0–19 years) who underwent HCT and developed a laboratory-confirmed RSV infection between 2010 and 2019. Clinical characteristics, laboratory values, and immunosuppressive and transplant history were analyzed. Outcomes included new or increased supplemental oxygen requirement, RSV-related hospitalization, progression to lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), invasive mechanical ventilation, and 90-day mortality. Univariate logistic regression was used to screen candidate predictors, followed by the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) for variable selection, and multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors associated with clinical outcomes. Results Among 204 pediatric HCT recipients with RSV infection, 41.7% had RSV-related hospitalization, 21.2% required new or increased supplemental oxygen, and 4% required invasive mechanical ventilation within 28 days after the diagnosis. Mortality within 90 days was 5.4%, with one death attributable to RSV. In multivariable models, female sex, younger age (particularly <5 years), neutropenia (ANC <500/mm3), presence of co-pathogen in the respiratory tract and chronic lung disease were independently associated with this oxygen outcome, while non-peripheral graft sources and T-cell–depleting therapy were associated with RSV-related hospitalization. Conclusions Severe outcomes are common in pediatric HCT recipients with RSV infection. Younger age, markers of impaired immune recovery, history of chronic lung disease, and T-cell–depleting therapy are major determinants of adverse outcomes. These findings support targeted risk stratification and may inform preventive and treatment strategies in this high-risk population.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)在儿科造血细胞移植(HCT)受者中导致显著的发病率;然而,严重疾病的危险因素仍未完全明确。方法 我们在美国16家移植中心进行了一项多中心回顾性研究,评估了2010年至2019年间接受HCT并发生实验室确诊RSV感染的儿童和青少年(0–19岁)。分析了临床特征、实验室值、免疫抑制和移植史。结局包括新的或增加的辅助供氧需求、RSV相关住院、进展为下呼吸道感染(LRTI)、侵入性机械通气以及90天内的死亡率。使用单变量逻辑回归筛选候选预测因子,随后采用最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)进行变量选择,并通过多变量逻辑回归确定与临床结局独立相关的预测因子。结果 在204例RSV感染的儿科HCT受者中,41.7%发生了RSV相关住院,21.2%需要新的或增加的辅助供氧,4%需要侵入性机械通气,且在RSV感染后28天内。90天内的死亡率为5.4%,其中一例死亡归因于RSV。在多变量模型中,女性性别、年龄较小(特别是<5岁)、中性粒细胞减少(ANC <500/mm3)、呼吸道存在共感染病原体以及慢性肺病是与供氧需求独立相关的危险因素,而非外周移植物来源和T细胞耗竭疗法则与RSV相关住院有关。结论 在RSV感染的儿科HCT受者中,严重结局较为常见。年龄较小、免疫恢复受损的标志、慢性肺病史以及T细胞耗竭疗法是不良结局的主要决定因素。这些发现支持针对性的风险分层,并可能为该高危人群的预防和治疗策略提供依据。

papers.title: Awareness and acceptance of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination among pregnant women in Poland: Results of an internet-based survey.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, particularly among vulnerable groups such as preterm newborns and infants with underlying medical conditions. The approval of the RSVpreF vaccine for use during pregnancy offers a new strategy for reducing RSV-related morbidity in newborns. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women in Poland, identify factors influencing vaccine hesitancy, and evaluate knowledge regarding the benefits of RSV vaccination. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A Computer-Assisted Web Interview (CAWI) survey was conducted among 668 respondents in Poland. An anonymous questionnaire consisting of 23 questions was distributed via social media platforms between July 25 and August 1, 2024. Participants were recruited through Facebook groups and Instagram and included women who had recently given birth or were currently pregnant. RESULTS: Respondents with medical backgrounds more frequently provided correct answers to questions regarding RSV than those without medical training. For example, when asked about methods of treating RSV infection, 109 medical professionals (74.15%) answered correctly, compared with 251 non-medical respondents (48.18%; p < 0.001). Individuals with medical backgrounds and those who received information about vaccination from their physician were more likely to receive the RSV vaccine during pregnancy. In addition, women vaccinated against other diseases, such as influenza and pertussis, were more likely to choose RSV vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: Vaccination against RSV during pregnancy is an important strategy for protecting newborns against severe RSV infection and should be promoted as a public health measure. Our findings highlight the need for targeted educational initiatives and public health campaigns to increase awareness and improve vaccination coverage among pregnant women.

papers.title_zh: 波兰孕妇对呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)疫苗接种的认知和接受程度:一项基于互联网的调查结果
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, particularly among vulnerable groups such as preterm newborns and infants with underlying medical conditions. The approval of the RSVpreF vaccine for use during pregnancy offers a new strategy for reducing RSV-related morbidity in newborns. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess RSV vaccination coverage among pregnant women in Poland, identify factors influencing vaccine hesitancy, and evaluate knowledge regarding the benefits of RSV vaccination. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A Computer-Assisted Web Interview (CAWI) survey was conducted among 668 respondents in Poland. An anonymous questionnaire consisting of 23 questions was distributed via social media platforms between July 25 and August 1, 2024. Participants were recruited through Facebook groups and Instagram and included women who had recently given birth or were currently pregnant. RESULTS: Respondents with medical backgrounds more frequently provided correct answers to questions regarding RSV than those without medical training. For example, when asked about methods of treating RSV infection, 109 medical professionals (74.15%) answered correctly, compared with 251 non-medical respondents (48.18%; p < 0.001). Individuals with medical backgrounds and those who received information about vaccination from their physician were more likely to receive the RSV vaccine during pregnancy. In addition, women vaccinated against other diseases, such as influenza and pertussis, were more likely to choose RSV vaccination. CONCLUSIONS: Vaccination against RSV during pregnancy is an important strategy for protecting newborns against severe RSV infection and should be promoted as a public health measure. Our findings highlight the need for targeted educational initiatives and public health campaigns to increase awareness and improve vaccination coverage among pregnant women.

papers.title: Relevance of Seasonal Revaccination against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Hematology Patients: First Insights in Stem Cell Transplant Recipients
papers.abstract: Abstract Several vaccines against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) have been commercialized recently. Their immediate immunogenicity in various conditions of immunosuppression, including patients receiving allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), have been reported in 2025 by different teams, including ours. In immunocompromised patients, the duration of vaccinal humoral protection as well as the relevance of seasonal revaccination is still unknown. By analyzing the kinetics of humoral responses after a single dose of bivalent RSVpreF vaccine over 12 months in 71 HSCT recipients, we show that annual revaccination benefits mostly those primarily vaccinated within the early 18 months after HSCT. We also provide a first evaluation of vaccinal clinical effectiveness in HSCT patients.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 近年来,针对呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的几种疫苗已被商业化。不同团队,包括我们团队,已在2025年报告了这些疫苗在不同免疫抑制状态下的即时免疫原性,包括接受异基因造血干细胞移植(HSCT)的患者。在免疫功能低下的患者中,疫苗诱导的体液免疫保护持续时间以及季节性加强接种的相关性仍不清楚。通过分析71名HSCT受者在单次接种双价RSVpreF 疫苗后12个月内的体液免疫反应动力学,我们发现年度加强接种主要对在HSCT后早期18个月内首次接种的患者有益。我们还首次评估了HSCT患者中疫苗的临床有效性。

papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV)–An Urgent Priority in Respiratory Disease Prevention
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, young children, older adults, and individuals with cardiopulmonary comorbidities or immunocompromised states. Recent advances enable layered prevention through maternal vaccination for infant protection, long-acting monoclonal antibodies for newborns and select toddlers, and vaccines for older adults. However, inequities in surveillance, seasonality-driven timing, and challenges in affordability and delivery—particularly in low- and middle-income countries— impede equitable uptake. This editorial underscores priority populations, synthesizes current evidence and policy directions, and outlines actionable levers in financing, procurement, and integrated maternal–child health delivery to accelerate access, making RSV prevention an urgent and achievable global health priority.

papers.title: Clinical Outcomes of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Versus Influenza Pneumonia in Critically Ill Adults
papers.abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza can both cause severe viral pneumonia requiring intensive care. Influenza is supported by established vaccination programs and antiviral therapy, whereas outcomes of RSV infection among critically ill adults remain less well characterized. This study compared clinical presentation, treatment, and outcomes between ICU admissions classified as RSV pneumonia and those classified as influenza pneumonia. Methods: A retrospective cohort was assembled from MIMIC-IV data covering 2008–2019. The analytical cohort comprised 201 infection-specific ICU observations classified as RSV pneumonia (n = 40) or influenza pneumonia (n = 161). Demographic characteristics, clinical measurements, treatments, and hospital outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association between infection type and in-hospital mortality, with adjustment for age, sex, and serum lactate. Internal model validation used 300 bootstrap resamples. Results: The RSV group was older than the influenza group (66.7 vs. 59.1 years; p = 0.009), had a longer ICU stay (median 3.0 [IQR 2.0–7.0] vs. 2.0 [IQR 1.0–4.0] days; p = 0.003), and had a higher admission heart rate (p = 0.009). papers.title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus–Related Hospitalizations Among Infants Receiving Nirsevimab
papers.abstract: Importance Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization among infants. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody that protects against severe RSV, was publicly funded for all infants in the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Quebec starting in the fall of 2024. Objective To estimate the clinical effectiveness of nirsevimab at preventing RSV-related emergency department (ED) visits, inpatient hospitalizations, and intensive care unit (ICU) admissions. Design, Setting, and Participants This test-negative case-control study obtained data from 7 tertiary care pediatric hospitals located in Ontario and Quebec, Canada, that are members of the Surveillance Program for the Rapid Identification and Tracking of Infectious Diseases in Kids (SPRINT-KIDS) Project. Symptomatic infants younger than 12 months who were tested for RSV in the ED, inpatient units, or ICUs of participating institutions between October 27, 2024, and March 1, 2025, were included. Exposure Receipt of nirsevimab 7 days or more prior to RSV test date. Main Outcome and Measure The primary outcome was laboratory-confirmed RSV infection. Participants were stratified by disposition outcome—ED visit only, hospitalization, or ICU admission—on the day of specimen collection or within the subsequent 14 days. Results Among the 1942 eligible encounters in infants (median [IQR] age, 3.0 [1.9-5.6] months; 1110 males [57.2%]) who were tested for RSV, 683 (35.2%) had RSV-positive test results (cases) and 1259 (64.8%) had RSV-negative test results (controls). Overall, 429 infants (22.1%) received nirsevimab. A lower proportion of cases than controls received nirsevimab (7.0% [48 of 683] vs 30.3% [381 of 1259]; P < .001). Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against laboratory-confirmed RSV was estimated to be 78% (95% CI, 68%-84%), including 77% (95% CI, 62%-86%) against ED visits, 79% (95% CI, 66%-87%) against hospitalizations, and 97% (95% CI, 85%-100%) against ICU admissions. Effectiveness remained high across all subgroups, including premature infants (90% [95% CI, 66%-98%]), those with comorbidities (86% [95% CI, 37%-98%]), and time from receipt (85% [95% CI, 75%-92%]); results of sensitivity analyses were consistent with those of primary analysis. Conclusions and Relevance This test-negative case-control study found that administration of nirsevimab to infants had high estimated effectiveness in preventing RSV disease severity that requires hospital-based care. The results suggest that nirsevimab has the potential to reduce the burden of RSV.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在估计尼塞韦单抗在预防婴儿RSV相关住院方面的效果,以应对减少RSV负担的需求,因为RSV是该年龄段住院的主要原因之一。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在加拿大安大略省和魁北克省的7家三级儿童专科医院进行,研究对象为2024年10月27日至2025年3月1日期间接受RSV检测的婴儿。
elements_zh.methods: 婴儿根据样本采集当天或随后14天内的处置结果进行分层,包括仅急诊科就诊、住院或ICU入院。研究纳入了接受RSV检测的、年龄小于12个月的有症状婴儿,重点关注那些接种了尼塞韦单抗的婴儿。
elements_zh.main_results: Among 1942 eligible encounters, 683 (35.2%) had RSV-positive test results (cases) and 1259 (64.8%) had RSV-negative test results (controls). A lower proportion of cases than controls received nirsevimab (7.0% vs 30.3%; P < .001). The effectiveness of nirsevimab was estimated to be 78% (95% CI, 68%-84%), including 77% against ED visits, 79% against hospitalizations, and 97% against ICU admissions.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,尼塞韦单抗在预防需要住院治疗的RSV疾病严重程度方面具有较高的估计效果,且在所有亚组和接种后的时间中结果保持一致。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,尼塞韦单抗有可能减轻RSV的负担,特别是在预防需要住院的严重结果方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其测试阴性病例对照研究的设计,这可能引入偏倚。然而,尼塞韦单抗在所有亚组和接种后的时间中均表现出较高的效果,支持了研究结果的稳健性。

papers.source_body_en: Importance Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization among infants. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody that protects against severe RSV, was publicly funded for all infants in the Canadian provinces of Ontario and Quebec starting in the fall of 2024. Objective To estimate the clinical effectiveness of nirsevimab at preventing RSV-related emergency department (ED) visits, inpatient hospitalizations, and intensive care unit (ICU) admissions. Design, Setting, and Participants This test-negative case-control study obtained data from 7 tertiary care pediatric hospitals located in Ontario and Quebec, Canada, that are members of the Surveillance Program for the Rapid Identification and Tracking of Infectious Diseases in Kids (SPRINT-KIDS) Project. Symptomatic infants younger than 12 months who were tested for RSV in the ED, inpatient units, or ICUs of participating institutions between October 27, 2024, and March 1, 2025, were included. Exposure Receipt of nirsevimab 7 days or more prior to RSV test date. Main Outcome and Measure The primary outcome was laboratory-confirmed RSV infection. Participants were stratified by disposition outcome—ED visit only, hospitalization, or ICU admission—on the day of specimen collection or within the subsequent 14 days. Results Among the 1942 eligible encounters in infants (median [IQR] age, 3.0 [1.9-5.6] months; 1110 males [57.2%]) who were tested for RSV, 683 (35.2%) had RSV-positive test results (cases) and 1259 (64.8%) had RSV-negative test results (controls). Overall, 429 infants (22.1%) received nirsevimab. A lower proportion of cases than controls received nirsevimab (7.0% [48 of 683] vs 30.3% [381 of 1259]; P < .001). Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against laboratory-confirmed RSV was estimated to be 78% (95% CI, 68%-84%), including 77% (95% CI, 62%-86%) against ED visits, 79% (95% CI, 66%-87%) against hospitalizations, and 97% (95% CI, 85%-100%) against ICU admissions. Effectiveness remained high across all subgroups, including premature infants (90% [95% CI, 66%-98%]), those with comorbidities (86% [95% CI, 37%-98%]), and time from receipt (85% [95% CI, 75%-92%]); results of sensitivity analyses were consistent with those of primary analysis. Conclusions and Relevance This test-negative case-control study found that administration of nirsevimab to infants had high estimated effectiveness in preventing RSV disease severity that requires hospital-based care. The results suggest that nirsevimab has the potential to reduce the burden of RSV.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在估计尼塞韦单抗在预防婴儿RSV相关住院方面的效果,以应对减少RSV负担的需求,因为RSV是该年龄段住院的主要原因之一。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在加拿大安大略省和魁北克省的7家三级儿童专科医院进行,研究对象为2024年10月27日至2025年3月1日期间接受RSV检测的婴儿。
analysis_zh.methods: 婴儿根据样本采集当天或随后14天内的处置结果进行分层,包括仅急诊科就诊、住院或ICU入院。研究纳入了接受RSV检测的、年龄小于12个月的有症状婴儿,重点关注那些接种了尼塞韦单抗的婴儿。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究发现,尼塞韦单抗在预防需要住院治疗的RSV疾病严重程度方面具有较高的估计效果,且在所有亚组和接种后的时间中结果保持一致。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,尼塞韦单抗有可能减轻RSV的负担,特别是在预防需要住院的严重结果方面。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其测试阴性病例对照研究的设计,这可能引入偏倚。然而,尼塞韦单抗在所有亚组和接种后的时间中均表现出较高的效果,支持了研究结果的稳健性。

papers.title: Rapid subtype-specific detection of respiratory syncytial virus A and B using an RNase HII-dependent RT-LAMP lateral flow assay
papers.abstract: Introduction Rapid and simultaneous detection of respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV A) and RSV B with subtype discrimination is important for point-of-care (POC) diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance. Methods We developed the RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay, a duplex reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) system combined with nucleic acid lateral flow (NALF) detection for simultaneous subtype-specific detection of RSV A and RSV B from nasopharyngeal swab specimens. To improve specificity during multiplex RT-LAMP, blocked inner primers, activated by RNase HII, were incorporated to suppress non-specific amplification. Subtype-specific detection was achieved on a single PCRD multiplex strip using 5′-FAM–and 5′-DIG–labeled loop primers for RSV A (T1 line) and RSV B (T2 line), respectively. Results The analytical limit of detection was 4 × 10 1 copies/μL using plasmid DNA standards. In clinical specimen dilution series, the assay detected RSV down to the 10 −3 dilution in clinical specimens, showing sensitivity approaching that of the comparator RT-PCR assay. Clinical validation was performed using 281 archived nasopharyngeal swab specimens (87 RSV A-positive, 94 RSV B-positive, and 100 RSV-negative), with the AllplexTM Respiratory Panel 1 assay used as the reference method. The RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay demonstrated sensitivities of 95.4% (95% CI: 88.8%–98.2%) for RSV A and 97.9% (95% CI: 92.6%–99.4%) for RSV B, with no false-positive results observed in the 100 RSV-negative specimens. These results were comparable to those of the AllplexTM SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV assay (RSV A: 95.4%; RSV B: 98.9%) and higher than those of the STANDARD Q RSV Ag Test (RSV A: 82.8%; RSV B: 92.6%). Limited cross-subtype reactivity was observed in one RSV A-positive specimen and one RSV B-positive specimen, both of which showed dual T1/T2 signals on the lateral flow strip. No cross-reactive signals were observed in 42 specimens representing 14 common respiratory pathogens other than RSV. Discussion Overall, the RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay provides a rapid, accurate, and subtype-specific POC diagnostic platform for RSV detection and surveillance.

We developed the RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay, a duplex reverse transcription loop-mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) system combined with nucleic acid lateral flow (NALF) detection for simultaneous subtype-specific detection of RSV A and RSV B from nasopharyngeal swab specimens. To improve specificity during multiplex RT-LAMP, blocked inner primers, activated by RNase HII, were incorporated to suppress non-specific amplification. Subtype-specific detection was achieved on a single PCRD multiplex strip using 5′-FAM–and 5′-DIG–labeled loop primers for RSV A (T1 line) and RSV B (T2 line), respectively. The analytical limit of detection was 4 × 10 1 copies/μL using plasmid DNA standards. In clinical specimen dilution series, the assay detected RSV down to the 10 −3 dilution in clinical specimens, showing sensitivity approaching that of the comparator RT-PCR assay. Clinical validation was performed using 281 archived nasopharyngeal swab specimens (87 RSV A-positive, 94 RSV B-positive, and 100 RSV-negative), with the AllplexTM Respiratory Panel 1 assay used as the reference method. The RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay demonstrated sensitivities of 95.4% (95% CI: 88.8%–98.2%) for RSV A and 97.9% (95% CI: 92.6%–99.4%) for RSV B, with no false-positive results observed in the 100 RSV-negative specimens. These results were comparable to those of the AllplexTM SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV assay (RSV A: 95.4%; RSV B: 98.9%) and higher than those of the STANDARD Q RSV Ag Test (RSV A: 82.8%; RSV B: 92.6%). Limited cross-subtype reactivity was observed in one RSV A-positive specimen and one RSV B-positive specimen, both of which showed dual T1/T2 signals on the lateral flow strip. No cross-reactive signals were observed in 42 specimens representing 14 common respiratory pathogens other than RSV. Overall, the RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay provides a rapid, accurate, and subtype-specific POC diagnostic platform for RSV detection and surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a rapid and simultaneous detection method for respiratory syncytial virus A (RSV A) and RSV B with subtype discrimination, important for point-of-care diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved developing the RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay using nasopharyngeal swab specimens from 281 archived clinical samples, including 87 RSV A-positive, 94 RSV B-positive, and 100 RSV-negative specimens, with the AllplexTM Respiratory Panel 1 assay as the reference method.
analysis.methods: The RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay incorporated blocked inner primers activated by RNase HII to suppress non-specific amplification, and used 5′-FAM– and 5′-DIG–labeled loop primers for RSV A and RSV B detection on a single PCRD multiplex strip.
analysis.main_results: The assay achieved an analytical limit of detection of 4 × 10^1 copies/μL and demonstrated sensitivities of 95.4% (95% CI: 88.8%–98.2%) for RSV A and 97.9% (95% CI: 92.6%–99.4%) for RSV B, with no false-positive results in 100 RSV-negative specimens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay provided rapid, accurate, and subtype-specific point-of-care diagnostics for RSV detection and surveillance, comparable to or better than other commercial assays.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The assay can improve the accuracy and speed of RSV detection, aiding in point-of-care diagnostics and epidemiological surveillance, particularly in resource-limited settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of archived specimens and the need for further validation in real-time clinical settings. analysis.summary_en: This study developed a rapid and accurate RSV A/B rh-RT-LAMP-NALF assay for simultaneous subtype-specific detection, demonstrating high sensitivity and specificity in clinical specimens. The assay provides a valuable tool for point-of-care diagnostics and surveillance.

papers.full_text: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) significantly affects infants and vulnerable populations. Monoclonal antibodies (mAbs), together with vaccine strategies, mark progress in RSV prevention, necessitating ongoing monitoring of viral evolution and resistance. Methods RSV-positive upper respiratory tract samples from patients who tested positive for RSV between October 2023 and March 2025 were collected. Whole genomes were obtained using amplicon protocol, sequenced on Illumina platforms, and assembled with vcf-consensus-builder. Maximum-likelihood trees (IQ-TREE; GTR + F+I+G6/G4) and Bayesian coalescent methods (GTR + F+I+G6/G4; constant population and strict molecular clock) defined clades and large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs: posterior probability = 1, sequences > 10). Amino acid variability in nucleoprotein (N) and fusion protein (F), targets of the small-molecule inhibitor zelicapavir and the mAbs, was investigated. Multivariable analysis compared 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons. Results 302 RSV sequences (129 from 2023 to 2024, 173 from 2024 to 2025), mostly from infants (≤ 1 year, 56.0%) and males (57.3%), were retrieved; 72.7% of cases had lower-respiratory-tract infections, 67.2% were hospitalized, 15.0% were intensive-care-unit (ICU)-admitted, and 17 were nirsevimab breakthrough infections (N_BI). The most frequent clades were A.D.3 (26.8%) and B.D.E.1 (20.2%), followed by A.D.1.2 (17.5%) and A.D.5.2 (14.2%). Four LPCs were identified: two of 56 A.D.3 and 17 A.D.1.2 strains were detected exclusively in 2024–2025. mAb resistance-associated mutations were identified in two 2023–2024 and two 2024–2025 samples (palivizumab: K272E in A.D.5.3 and N262Y in A.D.3; nirsevimab: N208D in B.D.E.1 and K68I plus L204S in a B.D.E.1 N_BI). Among the 17 N_BI, the F antigenic site Ø S213R was also detected in an A.D.1.2 sample. No clesrovimab resistance was detected, though four mutations (three in 2024–2025 season) were found at its binding site (K433R in B.D.4.1.1; C439R in A.D.1.2; N437S in A.D.5.2; N444S in A.D.3). The N-I129M substitution associated with zelicapavir resistance was detected with an intrapatient relative-abundance of 0.05 in a 2024–2025 B.D.E.1 sample. By multivariable analysis, the 2024–2025 season was associated with an increased number of sequences in LPCs, increased F site Ø variability and Ct values, and fewer ICU entries (P < 0.05). Conclusions RSV genomic surveillance in Lombardy revealed ongoing viral diversification and F protein variability, underscoring the need for continuous monitoring to inform prophylaxis strategies. Acknowledgements The authors thank the staff of the Microbiology Laboratory at Fondazione IRCCS Ca’ Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico and Fondazione IRCCS Policlinico San Matteo Pavia for their outstanding technical support in sample processing, laboratory analyses, and data management. We also thank Beatrice Zita Passerini for her participation in the initial setup of the study. Funding This manuscript is financially supported by Fondo Beneficenza Intesa San Paolo (funded project: B/2023/0181). It is also partially supported by Unione Europea-Next Generation EU, Missione 4 Componente 1 CUP 2022MNXLE7. The funders had no role in study design, data collection, analysis, decision to publish, or manuscript preparation. Ethics declarations Ethics approval and consent to participate The study protocol was approved by the Ethics Committee of Lombardy Region CET 1 (prot. 0022943/2024) and was conducted in accordance with the principles of the 1964 Declaration of Helsinki and applicable national regulations. Written informed consent was obtained for prospectively collected biological samples whenever applicable. For retrospectively collected residual biological material and associated clinical data, the requirement for informed consent was waived in accordance with Article 110 of the Italian Personal Data Protection Code. Consent for publication Not applicable. Competing interests The authors declare no competing interests. papers.title_original: Genomic characterization of circulating respiratory syncytial virus strains in Lombardy before and after the introduction of nirsevimab prophylaxis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to assess the impact of nirsevimab prophylaxis on the genomic evolution of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) strains in Lombardy, addressing the need for ongoing monitoring of viral diversification and resistance to inform prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study analyzed RSV-positive upper respiratory tract samples collected from patients between October 2023 and March 2025, focusing on sequences from infants and individuals with lower-respiratory-tract infections.
analysis.methods: Whole genomes were obtained using an amplicon protocol, sequenced on Illumina platforms, and assembled with vcf-consensus-builder. Phylogenetic analysis was conducted using maximum-likelihood trees and Bayesian coalescent methods to define clades and large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs).
analysis.main_results: A total of 302 RSV sequences were retrieved, with 72.7% of cases involving lower-respiratory-tract infections, 67.2% requiring hospitalization, and 15.0% admitted to the intensive-care-unit (ICU). Additionally, 17 nirsevimab breakthrough infections (N_BI) were identified, and four large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs) were found, including two new LPCs in the 2024–2025 season.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of ongoing viral diversification and increased F protein variability, which highlights the importance of genomic surveillance to adapt prophylaxis strategies. This study provides novel insights into the temporal changes in RSV strains in Lombardy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the necessity of continuous genomic surveillance to monitor RSV evolution and resistance, which can inform the development and optimization of prophylaxis strategies, particularly for nirsevimab.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a specific geographic region and time period, and the evidence is based on genomic data without direct clinical outcomes. The confidence in the findings is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the genomic evolution of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Lombardy before and after the introduction of nirsevimab prophylaxis. RSV-positive upper respiratory tract samples were collected between October 2023 and March 2025, and whole genomes were sequenced and analyzed using phylogenetic methods. The results showed that 302 RSV sequences were retrieved, with a majority from infants and males, and 72.7% of cases involving lower-respiratory-tract infections. The study identified four large phylogenetic clusters (LPCs), including two new ones in the 2024–2025 season, and found increased variability in the F protein and fewer ICU admissions in the latter period. The authors concluded that ongoing genomic surveillance is essential to monitor RSV diversification and inform prophylaxis strategies. The study's findings are significant for understanding the impact of nirsevimab on viral evolution but are limited by the geographic and temporal scope of the data, resulting in moderate confidence in the conclusions.

papers.title: Structural evolution of ionizable lipids for nucleic acid delivery.
papers.abstract: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles have emerged as a potent non-viral delivery platform for nucleic acid therapeutics, achieving clinical breakthroughs ranging from the FDA-approved small interfering RNA therapeutic to mRNA vaccines against coronavirus disease 2019 and respiratory syncytial virus. Their success stems from the ability of ionizable lipids to remain neutral in physiological environments, yet protonate in acidic endosomes, enabling the efficient release of genetic cargo. Over the last several decades, their structures have evolved extensively through the application of combinatorial chemistry, rational design, incorporation of functional elements and, most recently, machine learning and artificial intelligence-guided strategies. These innovations have expanded ionizable lipids from passive carriers into multifunctional materials capable of organ-specific targeting, responsiveness, immunomodulation and theranostics. In this Review, we highlight the development, synthesis and structural evolution of ionizable lipids as well as their emerging on-demand design functionalities and next-generation biomedical applications. We provide insights into the challenges and gaps for translation, manufacturing and expansion of lipid nanoparticle-mediated nucleic acid therapeutics for precision RNA medicine.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 可电离脂质纳米颗粒已发展成为一种强大的非病毒核酸治疗药物递送平台,从FDA批准的小干扰RNA治疗药物到针对冠状病毒病2019和疫苗的mRNA 呼吸道合胞病毒,均取得了临床突破。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 在过去的几十年中,通过组合化学、理性设计、功能元素的引入以及最近的机器学习和人工智能指导策略,它们的结构经历了广泛的演变。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 这些创新使可电离脂质从被动载体转变为具有器官特异性靶向、响应性、免疫调节和诊疗功能的多功能材料。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在这篇综述中,我们强调了可电离脂质的发展、合成及其结构进化,以及它们的新兴按需设计功能和下一代生物医学应用。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 我们还提供了关于脂质纳米颗粒介导的核酸治疗向精准RNA医学转化、制造和扩展所面临的挑战和空白的见解。

papers.title: Healthcare resource use and costs following RSV-related hospitalizations among US adults aged 50 years and older.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), a common virus causing acute respiratory illness (ARI), can lead to severe disease among adults aged ≥50 y. We assessed healthcare resource utilization (HRU) and costs among United States (US) adults aged ≥50 y after hospitalization with RSV-ARI. Using 2015-2023 US claims data from the Optum® Clinformatics® Data Mart, three cohorts of patients aged ≥50 y were identified: patients with ≥1 RSV-ARI episode involving hospitalization (RSV-ARI cohort), patients with ≥1 influenza-ARI episode involving hospitalization (influenza-ARI cohort), and patients without recent ARI (control cohort). HRU and costs per-patient-per-month (PPPM) were assessed at 30 d, 3 months, and 1 y post-index. Adjusted regression models compared outcomes across cohorts. Overall, 14,759 patients were included in the RSV-ARI cohort, 77,468 in the influenza-ARI cohort, and 73,795 in the control cohort. The RSV-ARI cohort had significantly higher HRU vs. controls within 1 y post-index; adjusted incidence rate ratios (95% confidence interval) 30 d through 1 y post-index ranged from 81.07 (75.85, 86.65) to 11.56 (11.20, 11.93) for inpatient stays, 5.93 (5.58, 6.30) to 2.19 (2.09, 2.29) for emergency department visits, and 1.99 (1.95, 2.04) to 1.78 (1.75, 1.81) for outpatient visits. Adjusted total costs PPPM were higher for the RSV-ARI cohort vs. controls post-index (difference at 30 d: $37,025 [$36,345, $37,704]; 1 y: $6,699 [$6,476, $6,922]). HRU and costs among patients aged ≥50 y with RSV-ARI were higher vs. controls and generally similar between the RSV-ARI and influenza-ARI cohorts, demonstrating economic burden of severe RSV disease and the importance of RSV prevention.

papers.title: Testing the feasibility of a national respiratory swabbing tool in FluSurvey to support pandemic preparedness in England, 2025-26
papers.abstract: Background: FluSurvey is a participatory surveillance system, through which participants report weekly respiratory symptoms, healthcare use and social contacts. To support rapid public health assessment we developed a respiratory self-swabbing feature. We aimed to assess the feasibility of self-swabbing among symptomatic FluSurvey participants. Methods FluSurvey self-swabbing was deployed in England between January-March 2026. Adults reporting recent Acute Respiratory Infection symptoms were eligible for a self-swabbing Covid-19, RSV and Influenza PCR test which was returned to the laboratory by post. Participants were sent optional feedback surveys. We described swabbing interest, timeliness and participant demographics. We evaluated participant feedback to improve the process. Results There were 234 eligible illnesses during the study period; 45.7% (107/234) requested test kits and 93.5%(100/107) test kits were returned. Of these, 97.0%(97/100) had valid results; median participant age was 61.74 years (IQR:47.4-67.4), 68.4% were female and 90.0% were of white ethnicity. All nine regions in England were represented. Timeliness was high; the median time from symptom onset to specimen date was 4.0 days (IQR:3.0-5.0). Of participants completing feedback surveys, 96.7%(59/61) would consider participating in self-swabbing again. Conclusions We developed a tool to test individuals, often not presenting to healthcare, for respiratory viruses using an established community-based surveillance system. This tool can be rapidly deployed and adapted to public health need, to assess community-based emerging respiratory or pandemic infections. The high return rate and positive feedback suggest continued engagement of the cohort in respiratory virus swabbing.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:FluSurvey是一个参与式监测系统,通过该系统参与者每周报告呼吸道症状、医疗使用和社会接触情况。为支持快速公共卫生评估,我们开发了呼吸道自我拭子功能。我们的目标是评估自我拭子在有症状的FluSurvey参与者中的可行性。方法:FluSurvey自我拭子功能于2026年1月至3月在英格兰部署。报告近期急性呼吸道感染症状的成年人有资格获得自我拭子的Covid-19、RSV和流感PCR检测套件,通过邮寄方式送回实验室。参与者被发送可选的反馈调查问卷。我们描述了拭子兴趣、及时性和参与者的人口统计学特征。我们评估了参与者的反馈以改进流程。结果:研究期间共有234例符合条件的疾病;45.7%(107/234)请求了检测套件,其中93.5%(100/107)送回了套件。这些送回的套件中,97.0%(97/100)提供了有效结果;参与者的中位年龄为61.74岁(IQR:47.4-67.4),68.4%为女性,90.0%为白人种族。英格兰的九个地区均有代表。及时性较高;从症状出现到样本日期的中位时间是4.0天(IQR:3.0-5.0)。完成反馈调查的参与者中,96.7%(59/61)表示会考虑再次参与自我拭子。结论:我们开发了一个工具,利用已有的社区基础监测系统,对通常不前往医疗机构的个体进行呼吸道病毒检测。该工具可以快速部署和适应公共卫生需求,用于评估基于社区的新兴呼吸道或流行病学感染。高回收率和积极反馈表明队列研究在呼吸道病毒拭子检测中的持续参与,这可能为未来的公共卫生策略提供信息。

papers.title: Airway protease availability governs a reversible shift between syncytial and cell-free spread.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Paramyxoviruses such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3) spread in the airway by releasing virions and by forming syncytia. Spread phenotypes are typically attributed to the fusion protein cleavage site, yet it remains unclear whether, and if so, how, host protease context biases syncytial versus cell-free spread. We compared RSV and HPIV3-two closely related viruses with overlapping epithelial tropism but distinct F cleavage-site composition (polybasic, furin-type for RSV versus a distinct, less polybasic cleavage-site motif for HPIV3)-in respiratory cell lines and primary airway cells under defined in vitro protease conditions. In multi-cycle infections, furin-dominant, trypsin-like-low environments produced the largest syncytia, whereas trypsin-like-high environments favored smaller syncytia and more cell-free spread. Adding exogenous TMPRSS2 shifted HPIV3 toward cell-free spread with minimal impact on RSV. Using serine protease inhibitors (SERPINs) as protease-selective inhibitors, we show that inhibiting specific proteases restricts infection and remodels syncytium architecture, consistent with protease switching. Together, these results indicate that host protease availability is a reversible control point for respiratory virus dissemination. This framework has direct implications for protease-targeting therapeutics. Selective inhibition may reroute fusion activation and shift spread modality toward more syncytia-associated cytopathic effects rather than uniformly suppressing dissemination. IMPORTANCE: Respiratory syncytial virus and human parainfluenza virus 3 are leading causes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis in infants, the elderly, and immunocompromised patients, and disease severity tracks with how efficiently these viruses spread through the airway. Spread has long been attributed to a fixed feature of the viral fusion protein. Here, we show instead that the host airway environment-specifically, the proteases that activate viral fusion proteins-acts as a reversible switch between two modes of spread: virus release and cell-to-cell fusion. Because this switch can be moved, protease-targeting drugs may not simply block infection but redirect how the virus spreads, with consequences for tissue damage. Recognizing protease availability as a controllable determinant of dissemination reframes how we think about respiratory virus pathogenesis and offers a rationale for tuning, rather than only suppressing, viral spread with host-directed therapeutics.

analysis.methods: The researchers used serine protease inhibitors (SERPINs) to selectively inhibit proteases and observed the effects on viral spread, including syncytium formation and cell-free dissemination, in controlled in vitro settings.

analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro conditions, and the evidence is based on abstract-only reporting, which suggests a moderate confidence level in the generalizability of findings to in vivo scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how host protease availability influences the spread of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3) in the airway. It challenges the traditional view that viral spread is determined solely by fixed features of the fusion protein, showing instead that the host protease environment acts as a reversible switch between syncytial and cell-free spread. The study compared these viruses in respiratory cell lines and primary airway cells under defined in vitro protease conditions, revealing that furin-dominant, trypsin-like-low environments promote larger syncytia, while trypsin-like-high environments favor smaller syncytia and more cell-free spread. Exogenous TMPRSS2 addition shifted HPIV3 toward cell-free spread with minimal impact on RSV. The findings suggest that protease-targeting drugs may not simply block infection but redirect how the virus spreads, with potential implications for reducing tissue damage. However, the study is limited to in vitro settings, and the evidence is based on abstract-only reporting, which suggests moderate confidence in the generalizability of results to in vivo scenarios.

papers.title_zh: 气道蛋白酶的可用性决定了合胞体和细胞自由传播之间的可逆转变。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Paramyxoviruses such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and human parainfluenza virus 3 (HPIV3) spread in the airway by releasing virions and by forming syncytia. Spread phenotypes are typically attributed to the fusion protein cleavage site, yet it remains unclear whether, and if so, how, host protease context biases syncytial versus cell-free spread. We compared RSV and HPIV3-two closely related viruses with overlapping epithelial tropism but distinct F cleavage-site composition (polybasic, furin-type for RSV versus a distinct, less polybasic cleavage-site motif for HPIV3)-in respiratory cell lines and primary airway cells under defined in vitro protease conditions. In multi-cycle infections, furin-dominant, trypsin-like-low environments produced the largest syncytia, whereas trypsin-like-high environments favored smaller syncytia and more cell-free spread. Adding exogenous TMPRSS2 shifted HPIV3 toward cell-free spread with minimal impact on RSV. Using serine protease inhibitors (SERPINs) as protease-selective inhibitors, we show that inhibiting specific proteases restricts infection and remodels syncytium architecture, consistent with protease switching. Together, these results indicate that host protease availability is a reversible control point for respiratory virus dissemination. This framework has direct implications for protease-targeting therapeutics. Selective inhibition may reroute fusion activation and shift spread modality toward more syncytia-associated cytopathic effects rather than uniformly suppressing dissemination. IMPORTANCE: Respiratory syncytial virus and human parainfluenza virus 3 are leading causes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis in infants, the elderly, and immunocompromised patients, and disease severity tracks with how efficiently these viruses spread through the airway. Spread has long been attributed to a fixed feature of the viral fusion protein. Here, we show instead that the host airway environment-specifically, the proteases that activate viral fusion proteins-acts as a reversible switch between two modes of spread: virus release and cell-to-cell fusion. Because this switch can be moved, protease-targeting drugs may not simply block infection but redirect how the virus spreads, with consequences for tissue damage. Recognizing protease availability as a controllable determinant of dissemination reframes how we think about respiratory virus pathogenesis and offers a rationale for tuning, rather than only suppressing, viral spread with host-directed therapeutics.

papers.title: Post-acute symptom persistence following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza in children
papers.abstract: Persistent symptoms following acute viral respiratory infections are increasingly recognized in children. While post-acute sequelae of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; long COVID) have been extensively studied, whether comparable post-acute morbidity occurs after other major respiratory viruses and whether clinical patterns differ across pathogens remains incompletely characterized. This retrospective cohort study included children aged 0 to 18 years with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction–confirmed SARS-CoV-2 (n = 1540), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; n = 2150), or influenza (n = 2050) infections evaluated between January 2020 and December 2024 at a tertiary university hospital system in Istanbul, Turkey. Persistent symptoms were assessed at clinician-documented follow-up visits 4 to 6 weeks after virological diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors for each pathogen. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Model calibration was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and discriminative ability by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Among 5740 children, persistent symptoms at 4 to 6 weeks were documented in 24.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 22.2–25.8) with RSV, 22.0% (95% CI = 19.9–24.1) with SARS-CoV-2, and 21.2% (95% CI = 19.4–23.0) with influenza ( P = .086). While overall post-acute prevalence was comparable across the 3 viruses, symptom profiles differed markedly: RSV-related post-acute morbidity was dominated by respiratory and feeding difficulties in young infants; SARS-CoV-2 predominantly produced neurocognitive and systemic complaints in school-aged children; and influenza was characterized by sustained systemic symptoms. Hypoxemia was the strongest predictor for RSV (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.4, 95% CI = 1.7–3.3), while age >6 years (aOR = 2.1, 95% CI = 1.5–2.9) and hospitalization (aOR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.4–2.6) were leading predictors for SARS-CoV-2. Age-stratified analyses demonstrated a significant virus × age interaction ( P P > .05). Inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results. Post-acute symptom persistence following pediatric viral respiratory infections is common and follows virus-specific patterns. Overall post-acute symptom prevalence was comparable across the 3 viruses, but symptom profiles were strikingly virus-specific and age-dependent. This direct comparison of 3 major respiratory viruses demonstrates that post-acute morbidity extends beyond SARS-CoV-2 and varies by pathogen and age. These findings support the development of pathogen-informed follow-up considerations.

papers.title_original: Post-acute symptom persistence following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza in children

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the prevalence and patterns of post-acute symptoms following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza in children, addressing the need to understand the extent and nature of post-acute morbidity beyond SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on children aged 0 to 18 years with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 (n = 1540), RSV (n = 2150), or influenza (n = 2050) infections, evaluated at a tertiary university hospital system in Istanbul, Turkey, from January 2020 to December 2024.
analysis.methods: Persistent symptoms were assessed at follow-up visits 4 to 6 weeks after virological diagnosis using multivariable logistic regression and inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis. Model calibration and discriminative ability were assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, respectively.
analysis.main_results: Among 5740 children, 24.0% (95% CI = 22.2–25.8) had persistent symptoms after RSV, 22.0% (95% CI = 19.9–24.1) after SARS-CoV-2, and 21.2% (95% CI = 19.4–23.0) after influenza. RSV-related post-acute morbidity was characterized by respiratory and feeding difficulties in young infants, SARS-CoV-2 by neurocognitive and systemic complaints in school-aged children, and influenza by sustained systemic symptoms.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that post-acute symptom persistence following pediatric viral respiratory infections is common and follows virus-specific patterns, extending beyond SARS-CoV-2 and varying by pathogen and age.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the development of pathogen-informed follow-up considerations and highlight the importance of understanding virus-specific post-acute morbidity in children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and the potential for residual confounding, but the consistent results from inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis suggest robustness.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated post-acute symptoms in children following SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza infections, finding that while overall post-acute prevalence was comparable across the three viruses, symptom profiles were virus-specific and age-dependent, emphasizing the need for pathogen-informed follow-up care.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒和流感感染后儿童的后急性期症状及其模式,以了解SARS-CoV-2以外的后急性期发病率的范围和性质。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本回顾性队列研究研究纳入了2020年1月至2024年12月期间在土耳其伊斯坦布尔一家三级大学医院系统中评估的0至18岁儿童,其SARS-CoV-2(n = 1540)、RSV(n = 2150)或流感(n = 2050)感染均通过逆转录聚合酶链反应(RT-PCR)确认。
elements_zh.methods: 在病毒学诊断后4至6周,通过临床记录的随访访问评估持续症状。使用多变量逻辑回归和逆概率加权敏感性分析进行分析。模型校准通过Hosmer-Lemeshow检验进行评估,模型区分能力通过接收者操作特征曲线下的面积(AUC)进行评估。
elements_zh.main_results: 在5740名儿童中,RSV感染后4至6周持续症状的有24.0%(95% CI = 22.2–25.8),SARS-CoV-2感染后为22.0%(95% CI = 19.9–24.1),流感感染后为21.2%(95% CI = 19.4–23.0)。RSV相关的后急性期发病率主要表现为婴幼儿的呼吸系统和喂养困难;SARS-CoV-2则主要表现为学龄儿童的神经认知和全身性症状;而流感则以持续的全身性症状为特征。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,儿童病毒性呼吸道感染后的后急性期症状持续普遍存在,且遵循特定病毒的模式,不仅限于SARS-CoV-2,且因病原体和年龄而异。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持制定基于病原体的随访考虑方案,并强调了了解儿童中特定病毒后急性期发病率的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计以及潜在的残留混杂因素,但逆概率加权敏感性分析的一致结果表明其结果具有稳健性。

papers.title_zh: SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒和流感后儿童急性症状持续存在
papers.source_body_en: Persistent symptoms following acute viral respiratory infections are increasingly recognized in children. While post-acute sequelae of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2; long COVID) have been extensively studied, whether comparable post-acute morbidity occurs after other major respiratory viruses and whether clinical patterns differ across pathogens remains incompletely characterized. This retrospective cohort study included children aged 0 to 18 years with reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction–confirmed SARS-CoV-2 (n = 1540), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; n = 2150), or influenza (n = 2050) infections evaluated between January 2020 and December 2024 at a tertiary university hospital system in Istanbul, Turkey. Persistent symptoms were assessed at clinician-documented follow-up visits 4 to 6 weeks after virological diagnosis. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors for each pathogen. Bonferroni correction was applied for multiple comparisons. Model calibration was assessed using the Hosmer-Lemeshow test, and discriminative ability by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Among 5740 children, persistent symptoms at 4 to 6 weeks were documented in 24.0% (95% confidence interval [CI] = 22.2–25.8) with RSV, 22.0% (95% CI = 19.9–24.1) with SARS-CoV-2, and 21.2% (95% CI = 19.4–23.0) with influenza ( P = .086). While overall post-acute prevalence was comparable across the 3 viruses, symptom profiles differed markedly: RSV-related post-acute morbidity was dominated by respiratory and feeding difficulties in young infants; SARS-CoV-2 predominantly produced neurocognitive and systemic complaints in school-aged children; and influenza was characterized by sustained systemic symptoms. Hypoxemia was the strongest predictor for RSV (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.4, 95% CI = 1.7–3.3), while age >6 years (aOR = 2.1, 95% CI = 1.5–2.9) and hospitalization (aOR = 1.9, 95% CI = 1.4–2.6) were leading predictors for SARS-CoV-2. Age-stratified analyses demonstrated a significant virus × age interaction ( P P > .05). Inverse probability weighting sensitivity analysis yielded consistent results. Post-acute symptom persistence following pediatric viral respiratory infections is common and follows virus-specific patterns. Overall post-acute symptom prevalence was comparable across the 3 viruses, but symptom profiles were strikingly virus-specific and age-dependent. This direct comparison of 3 major respiratory viruses demonstrates that post-acute morbidity extends beyond SARS-CoV-2 and varies by pathogen and age. These findings support the development of pathogen-informed follow-up considerations.

papers.title: Respiratory viral infections in patients with inherited metabolic disorders: Pathogen distribution and clinical outcomes.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Children with inborn errors of metabolism (IEMs) are at increased risk for severe viral infections, which may precipitate acute metabolic decompensation, PICU admission, and death. Pathogen specific outcomes in this population remain poorly defined. The objective was to evaluate the epidemiology, viral etiology, and clinical severity of respiratory viral infections in hospitalized children with IEMs. Method: This single-center retrospective study included children with IMDs hospitalized with acute infectious illness and laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral detection during 2018-2024. Demographic features, underlying metabolic diagnoses, viral pathogens, and outcomes were evaluated. Result: A total of 45 infection episodes among 41 children were included; median age was 4 years (IQR:0.5-9.5), and 31 patients (75.6%) were male. The most common IEMs categories were amino acid metabolism disorders (36.6%) and complex molecule degradation and processing defects (26.8%). Respiratory disease was the predominant presentation (77.8%), followed by gastroenteritis (8.9%), sepsis (6.7%), and meningoencephalitis (6.7%). Acute metabolic decompensation occurred in 11/23 infection episodes in metabolically vulnerable patients (47.8%). Influenza was the most frequently identified virus (35.6%), followed by rhinovirus (22.2%), seasonal coronavirus (sCoV) (13.3%), and respiratory syncytial virus (11.1%). PICU admission was required in 13.3% (6/45) of cases. Infection-related mortality was 6.7% (n = 3), and all fatal cases had sCoV infection. Conclusion: Influenza was the most frequently identified pathogen, while sCoV was detected in all three infection-related deaths. Our results suggest that respiratory viral infections may be associated with clinical burden in children with IMDs, highlighting the importance of close clinical monitoring and supportive management in this vulnerable population.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the epidemiology, viral etiology, and clinical severity of respiratory viral infections in hospitalized children with inherited metabolic disorders (IEMs), addressing the need for better understanding of pathogen-specific outcomes in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A single-center retrospective study was conducted on children with IEMs hospitalized with acute infectious illness and laboratory-confirmed respiratory viral detection during 2018-2024, involving 45 infection episodes among 41 children.
analysis.methods: The study evaluated demographic features, underlying metabolic diagnoses, viral pathogens, and outcomes using retrospective data.
analysis.main_results: A total of 45 infection episodes among 41 children were included; influenza was the most frequently identified virus (35.6%), followed by rhinovirus (22.2%), seasonal coronavirus (sCoV) (13.3%), and respiratory syncytial virus (11.1%). PICU admission was required in 13.3% (6/45) of cases, and infection-related mortality was 6.7% (n = 3), all due to sCoV infection.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study suggests that respiratory viral infections may be associated with a clinical burden in children with IEMs, highlighting the importance of close clinical monitoring and supportive management in this vulnerable population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that respiratory viral infections, particularly sCoV, may have significant clinical implications in children with IEMs, emphasizing the need for tailored management strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-center design and the retrospective nature of the data, which may affect generalizability. The sample size is relatively small, and the study does not include specific methods for identifying respiratory syncytial virus, which may introduce bias.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估住院遗传性代谢障碍(IEMs)患儿呼吸道病毒感染的流行病学、病毒病因及临床严重程度,以应对该人群中病原体特异性结局的理解需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究为单中心回顾性研究,纳入了2018年至2024年间因急性感染性疾病住院且实验室确认呼吸道病毒感染的IEMs患儿,共涉及41名患儿的45例感染事件。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究通过回顾性数据评估了人口学特征、基础代谢诊断、病毒病原体及结局。
elements_zh.main_results: 共纳入41名患儿的45例感染事件;流感是最常检测到的病毒(35.6%),其次是鼻病毒(22.2%)、季节性冠状病毒(sCoV)(13.3%)和呼吸道合胞病毒(11.1%)。需要PICU入院的病例占13.3%(6/45),与感染相关的死亡率为6.7%(n = 3),所有病例均因sCoV感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 本研究提示,呼吸道病毒感染可能与遗传性代谢障碍患儿的临床负担相关,强调了对这一脆弱人群进行密切临床监测和支持性管理的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,呼吸道病毒感染,尤其是sCoV,可能对遗传性代谢障碍患儿具有重要的临床意义,强调了需要制定针对性的管理策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其单中心设计和回顾性数据的性质,这可能影响结果的普遍适用性。样本量相对较小,且未包含用于识别呼吸道合胞病毒的具体方法,这可能引入偏倚。

papers.abstract_zh: 引言:先天性代谢错误(IEMs)患儿更容易发生严重的病毒感染,这可能导致急性代谢失代偿、PICU入院和死亡。该人群中的病原体特异性结局仍不明确。本研究旨在评估住院遗传性代谢障碍(IEMs)患儿呼吸道病毒感染的流行病学、病毒病因及临床严重程度。方法:本研究为单中心回顾性研究,纳入了2018年至2024年间因急性感染性疾病住院且实验室确认呼吸道病毒感染的IMD患儿,共45例感染事件。评估了人口学特征、基础代谢诊断、病毒病原体及结局。结果:共纳入41名患儿的45例感染事件;中位年龄为4岁(IQR:0.5-9.5),其中31例(75.6%)为男性。最常见的IEMs类别为氨基酸代谢障碍(36.6%)和复杂分子降解与处理缺陷(26.8%)。呼吸道疾病是最常见的临床表现(77.8%),其次是胃肠道炎(8.9%)、败血症(6.7%)和脑膜脑炎(6.7%)。在代谢脆弱的患者中,11/23例感染事件出现了急性代谢失代偿(47.8%)。流感是最常检测到的病毒(35.6%),其次是鼻病毒(22.2%)、季节性冠状病毒(sCoV)(13.3%)和呼吸道合胞病毒(11.1%)。需要PICU入院的病例占13.3%(6/45)。与感染相关的死亡率为6.7%(n = 3),所有致命病例均因sCoV感染。结论:流感是最常检测到的病原体,而sCoV在所有三例与感染相关的死亡病例中均有检测。我们的研究结果表明,呼吸道病毒感染可能与遗传性代谢障碍患儿的临床负担相关,强调了对这一脆弱人群进行密切临床监测和支持性管理的重要性。

papers.title: SARS-CoV-2 Coinfections and Severity in Hospitalized Children With Systematic Testing.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Co-circulation of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) with other respiratory viruses raised concerns that coinfections may increase pediatric coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity, but evidence is limited by variable testing practices. We assessed the epidemiology and outcomes of SARS-CoV-2 respiratory viral coinfections in hospitalized children. METHODS: We analyzed national surveillance data from the Canadian Immunization Monitoring Program, ACTive (IMPACT) COVID-19 study. Children aged <17 years hospitalized with confirmed COVID-19 during Delta and Omicron periods were included. Coinfection was defined as SARS-CoV-2 plus ≥1 additional respiratory virus. Primary analyses were restricted to centres with systematic multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of all admissions with acute respiratory illness (n = 5), while secondary analyses included all centres (n = 13). Associations with outcomes (respiratory support, ventilation, intensive care and severe COVID-19) were estimated using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression and adjusted odds ratios (aORs). RESULTS: Among 2831 hospitalized children, 938 were admitted at centers with systematic multiplex PCR testing, among whom 18.6% had ≥1 respiratory viral coinfection. Respiratory syncytial virus (39.7%) and enterovirus/rhinovirus (38.5%) coinfections were the most common. Coinfections were not associated with increased odds of severe COVID-19 in centers with systematic multiplex PCR testing (aOR 0.94; 95% confidence interval, 0.76-1.15). In secondary analyses including all centers irrespective of testing strategy, coinfections were associated with increased odds of severe COVID-19 (aOR 1.42; 95% confidence interval, 1.05-1.91). CONCLUSIONS: In centers that systematically conducted multiplex PCR testing, SARS-CoV-2 respiratory viral coinfections were not associated with increased COVID-19 severity. Differences observed when including centers without systematic testing underscore the importance of considering testing strategies when evaluating the clinical impact of coinfections.

Associations with outcomes (respiratory support, ventilation, intensive care and severe COVID-19) were estimated using multivariable mixed-effects logistic regression and adjusted odds ratios (aORs). Britannica Editors Last updated Sep. 10, 2026 •History Britannica AI Ask Anything Table of Contents Table of Contents Ask Anything News • Medical groups offer vaccine guidance to fill federal vacuum • Sep. 2, 2026, 10:00 AM ET (NPR) Show less respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), infectious agent of the respiratory system that typically produces a mild coldlike illness but in susceptible individuals, particularly infants under six months of age, is a major cause of severe and potentially fatal lower respiratory disease. Severe bronchiolitis and pneumonia caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) occurs most commonly in the elderly and in young children. An estimated 60 to 70 percent of children have been infected with RSV by age one, and nearly all children have been infected by age two. Because RSV effectively evades immunity, repeat infections are common. RSV infection is seasonal, occurring as an annual epidemic during the winter in most countries in temperate regions. What's the Difference Between Bacteria and Viruses?Knowing the difference isn't just a technical distinction—it can save lives.(more) See all videos for this article Direct person-to-person contact is thought to be the most common route of RSV transmission. The virus also can be transmitted through the air, such as by coughing or sneezing, and through direct contact with a contaminated surface followed by touching of the face. Symptoms generally appear within four to six days of infection and include runny nose, cough, sore throat, headache, fever, and wheezing. In instances of severe illness, affected individuals may have a high fever, severe wheezing, rapid or laboured breathing, and bluish lips or fingers. Infants may only show signs of irritability, fatigue, and breathing difficulties, even in severe cases. The only pharmacological therapy available for treatment of RSV is the nucleoside analogue ribavirin, which can be administered orally, parenterally (by injection or infusion), or by inhalation. An injectable humanized monoclonal antibody is available for prevention of severe RSV illness in high-risk infants and children. It provides passive immunity and must by given by intramuscular injection once a month during RSV season. Transmission can be prevented with frequent handwashing, cleaning of surfaces, avoiding close contact with others, and covering the mouth and nose with the upper arm when coughing or sneezing. news.content_zh: 2026年9月10日发表于Britannica.com的文章提供了关于呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的一般信息,RSV是一种呼吸道感染病原体。RSV通常引起轻微的类似感冒的症状,但在6个月以下的婴儿和老年人中可能导致严重的甚至致命的下呼吸道疾病。RSV具有季节性,在温带地区冬季会出现年度流行。文章指出,几乎所有儿童在两岁前都会感染RSV,由于病毒能够逃避免疫,重复感染很常见。治疗选项包括利巴韦林,可以通过口服、静脉注射或吸入给药,以及一种注射用的人源化单克隆抗体,用于高风险婴儿和儿童的预防。预防措施包括频繁洗手、清洁表面、避免密切接触以及咳嗽或打喷嚏时遮住口鼻。文章未报告任何特定的暴发或病例数,但概述了RSV的一般影响和应对策略。
